articles.title: Magic: The Gathering Designer's Response to Product Fatigue Sparks Debate About the Deluge of New Cards
articles.summary: There are a lot of Magic: The Gathering cards coming out these days, and there are a lot of Magic players who think there are too many. But fans don't need to pay attention to every set — according to Magic game designer Mark Rosewater.
body: Last night, Rosewater posted to his Tumblr to answer a question from a fan about the product fatique players feel from having six Magic sets every year. He replied: "We did some research on this. It turns out a very small minority of Magic players feels a need to track every newly released card. Obviously, this audience tends to be very enfranchised, so they’re over represented online."
"The game already has over 33,000 unique cards," he added. "We’re well past the mark where any one player can mentally track everything."

And it doesn't seem like Wizards of the Coast plans to slow things down any time soon, even if some enfranchised players — myself included — are sometimes fatigued by the sheer amount of cards that come out every year.

In the same blog post, Rosewater added: "Limiting how many cards we release per year to how many cards this small group can comfortably mentally track just doesn’t make good business sense. Our upper limit needs to be guided by what players are purchasing and playing, not by how easy it is to track everything new." So, essentially the deluge of new Magic cards will continue as long as sales support them.
points: There are a lot of Magic: The Gathering cards coming out these days, and there are a lot of Magic players who think there are too many.
But fans don't need to pay attention to every set — according to Magic game designer Mark Rosewater.

articles.title: Ocarina of Time Remake Will Support All Existing Zelda Amiibo With In-Game Item Bonuses
articles.summary: Nintendo just dropped a new overview trailer for the Ocarina of Time remake, offering a fresh look at revamped environments, characters, and combat. We had the chance to play some of the game ourselves, and were surprised by just how many changes Nintendo is making to the iconic N64 release.
body: While Nintendo previously announced two new amiibo figures tied to the remake - Young Link and Young Zelda - the new overview trailer also confirms support for all existing Zelda amiibo. It doesn’t go into too much detail about what that support will involve, but the trailer shows Link receiving a number of helpful items, including healing hearts, Green Potions, and a Deku Stick.

It appears players can tap existing Zelda amiibo for helpful consumables and items, but not necessarily any exclusive cosmetics or weapons. This is similar to how non-Zelda amiibo worked in Tears of the Kingdom, which allowed for daily “bonus” scans of general Amiibo once per day.
The previously announced Ocarina of Time amiibo, which are up for preorder with varying levels of stock across retailers, will net players wearable masks for Zelda and Link.

Nintendo first launched the amiibo product line with the Wii U. Each amiibo comes with a small figure as well as a card that you can scan from Nintendo consoles, netting players various unlocks and bonuses across games.

articles.title: Ubisoft’s Latest Restructuring Plan Puts Trials Developer RedLynx On The Chopping Block
articles.summary: Ubisoft has announced that it plans to shut down Trials developer RedLynx as part of its ongoing restructuring efforts, as well as reduce the workforce of its Skull and Bones studio, Ubisoft Singapore, by laying off 72 people.
body: Under Finnish law (via Kotaku ), Ubisoft is legally required to consult and negotiate with employees before it makes major changes to the studio, which is why Ubisoft hasn't officially announced yet that it will shut down RedLynx--although it's likely only a matter of time. The studio was first formed in 2000, and it's best known for its series of challenging--but highly enjoyable--Trials games, 2.5D motorcycle platforming games that require players to master their vehicle, gravity, and overcome a series of increasingly dangerous obstacle courses. Ubisoft acquired the studio in 2011, and RedLynx's Trials HD quickly became a breakout hit on the Xbox Arcade marketplace.

Several games in the Trails franchise have been released over the years, with the last one being Trials Rising in 2019. Since then, RedLynx assisted Massive Entertainment with the Google Stadia port of The Division 2 and the Switch 2 port of Star Wars Outlaws, and it also produced the 2023 mobile game Gwen's Getaway. Last year, RedLynx lost 60 staff members during a restructuring wave at Ubisoft and it was announced that it would pivot to making mobile games.

articles.title: GTA 6 Leaks Are Still Coming, Rockstar Labels The 2022 Hack “Weirdly Invasive”
articles.summary: Rockstar Games has reacted to the mass GTA 6 leaks, which began in 2022, with a top developer at the studio saying it "feels like somebody's wading through your dirty washing." Bloomberg published these comments from Rockstar developers on the same day that GTA 6 leaker CyberLeek posted yet another…
body: "It feels like somebody’s wading through your dirty washing,” Rockstar North's Aaron Garbut said. “It’s like they’re inside your head. You see your early work out there. Nobody’s ever supposed to see that. It’s really weirdly invasive. And so it’s quite hard to deal with on an emotional level.”
Rockstar and Take-Two eventually tracked down the hacker who was allegedly responsible for the leaks in 2022. This person will reportedly face court on November 9, just days before GTA 6 releases.

The hack pushed Rockstar to implement a controversial new policy requiring developers to work from the office, as opposed to remotely. Rockstar publishing boss Jennifer Kolbe said Rockstar will take another look at this policy after GTA 6 is released, but she doesn't envision major changes.

"The idea that we would have the game in that many environments is something that I think the security team would not love,” she said. “I think if we did not have a game that people wanted to steal as much, maybe it would be an easier conversation.”

articles.title: ‘We Vibe Coded a New Epic Games Launcher’ – Epic’s New Store App Was Built Using AI
articles.summary: Epic has revealed a newly refreshed version of the Epic Games Launcher, its Steam-like platform that provides access to the Epic Games Store, your games library, social features, and a developer’s hub.
body: “Programming is hard,” wrote Epic in a new blog post. “So, instead of doing that, we vibe coded a new Epic Games Launcher that’s way faster and more responsive than the current one, and has a new look.”

The term “vibe coding” is often used in a joke context to describe code developed entirely through AI prompts, rather than actual coding expertise. It’s interesting, then, to see Epic use the term in an announcement for its own product. But just how has the company approached the build of its new app?

During an interview with IGN, vice president and general manager of Epic Games Store Martin Keely discussed how the technology has been used. “We have used AI as a tool as part of our development process,” he said. “It's obviously an issue that's of high visibility at the moment across the industry, but for us, it made us more efficient and allowed a small team to rewrite the code base and be able to launch it faster across platforms, support Windows and Mac, and we're going to have a Linux version as well.”

articles.title: Netflix Lays Off Over 1,000 People, Around 6% of the Workforce
articles.summary: Netflix has laid off over 1,000 staff in its biggest cutbacks to date, amounting to around 6% of its workforce. The cuts will predominantly affect its product, technology, legal and HR teams.
body: “Our mission — to entertain the world — is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources,” co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters wrote in an email to employees, via WSJ.

“Our business is strong and growing, and we remain on track to deliver our full-year forecast. We’ll continue to invest aggressively in high-impact areas to improve our service and further drive growth and innovation. Doing that means making focused choices across the business so we can keep delivering for our members, partners, employees, and investors.”

Despite having a range of beloved exclusives, Netflix has struggled to keep up with audience demand lately, with some accusing it of adopting a quantity over quality approach. In a recently announced deal with Disney, Netflix plans to license shows from the rival streaming service to help meet demand.

Netflix has also attempted to break into gaming to increase dwell time on its service. Most famously, the GTA 6 Extended Look was a Netflix exclusive for the first few hours. By all accounts, it was a hit, breaking 31.1 million views in its first week.

articles.title: GTA 6 Could Have Been Even Bigger And Released Years Sooner, But Then These Things Happened
articles.summary: A big new report revealed more details about Rockstar's long-awaited GTA 6, including how the game's scope was originally much bigger and that the game could have released years sooner.
body: Bloomberg reported that when a small team from Rockstar traveled to Miami in 2015 to begin planning GTA 6, they envisioned the game spanning "big swaths of land across both North and South America." It was in development under the codename Project Americas at this time.

The report went on to say that Rockstar would pare down GTA 6's scope to include Miami and its surrounding areas instead of the original ambition. It's not a small world, though, as GTA 6's map is 3X bigger than the map in Rockstar's last game, 2018's Red Dead Redemption II. In addition to GTA 6's version of Miami with Vice City, the game takes players to a range of other locations in greater Leonida, which is a stand-in for Florida.

The report also digs into how Rockstar originally planned to develop GTA 6 concurrently with Red Dead Redemption II, which would have helped GTA 6 come to market sooner. However, as the scope for Red Dead Redemption II grew, Rockstar's Rob Nelson came to realize he needed to assign more staff at Rockstar's network of studios to help get the Western out the door in 2018.
points: A big new report revealed more details about Rockstar's long-awaited GTA 6, including how the game's scope was originally much bigger and that the game could have released years sooner.

articles.title: Hideo Kojima Reviews 2026’s Most Divisive Movie, Digger
articles.summary: After publishing his review of Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie, Hideo Kojima-who says his body is 70% made of movies--has posted his review of one of the most divisive mainstream films of the year.
body: Kojima said Digger is a "film that all of us living in today's world should see."
He added: "It is a work that remains with the audience, provoking reflection and sounding alarms."
Kojima doesn't get into detailed specifics in his Digger review, and that's likely because, if you've seen the movie or know the plot, you wouldn't want to spoil the film for other people, either.

In any event, Kojima said Digger and its message will stay with you for years to come. "As you absorb this film and carry it with you, a 'tool (a digger)' for delving deeper into the future will surely begin to take shape within you," he said.

articles.title: Over the Hill Just Invented the Cozy Driving Game and I'm in Love
articles.summary: Like Jusant, Over the Hill presents a clean, aspirational vision of an outdoorsy pastime, all smoothed and streamlined for maximum relaxing pleasure. Like Jusant, it's a meditative, peaceful game of exploration that's focused on taking it easy, reading the environment carefully, and being in the…
body: For this review of the indie offroad driving game Over the Hill, I was considering using a phrase along the lines of "the chill-out game of the year" in the headline, but this rang a niggling bell in my head. I looked it up, and sure enough, I'd used this exact framing three years ago for my preview of Don't Nod's excellent rock-climbing game Jusant. That's apt — Over the Hill inspires similar feelings in me, and I've compared the two games before.

In a way, Over the Hill is an even more minimal game. Jusant has a sparse, near-wordless narrative; Over the Hill doesn't even have that. Jusant is also a crafted, linear experience with a start and a definitive end. Over the Hill is just a sequence of large maps you can explore at will, dotted with things to discover and do. It's playable in four-player co-op, which I didn't get to try but imagine is a fun hangout experience. Played alone, though, it's a gloriously quiet and soothing experience.
points: Like Jusant, Over the Hill presents a clean, aspirational vision of an outdoorsy pastime, all smoothed and streamlined for maximum relaxing pleasure.

articles.title: Disney's Survival Thriller 'Whalefall' Proves How Hard It Is to Replicate 'The Martian'
articles.summary: Whalefall, Daniel Kraus’ 2023 novel about a scuba diver swallowed by a sperm whale, is often compared to Andy Weir’s 2011 book The Martian since both focus on men trapped alone in dire situations using all of their knowledge and skills to survive.
body: Jay’s recklessness is a symptom of his grief. The movie opens with Mitt jumping off his tour boat laden with weights so he can die in the ocean he loved rather than succumbing to mesothelioma in a hospital bed. It’s the most emotionally effective scene in the whole film, anchored by Brolin’s rasping breath as he prepares for his last dive. Hewey studiously ignores the suicide he’s assisting and focuses on fishing off the other side of the boat, before finally breaking down at the sound of the splash.

A year later, Jay still hasn’t read the note his dad left for him and can’t bring himself to visit the cemetery plot where his family buried an empty casket. Even though Mitt was very clear about his desire to nourish the ocean like a whale carcass – the eponymous whalefall – Jay is convinced that bringing back his remains will set things right.

articles.title: ArenaNet solves an ongoing Guild Wars 2 issue by ditching paid Living World add-ons and bundling them with expansions
articles.summary: ArenaNet has announced a major shift in its live service Guild Wars 2 operation today, ditching separate payments for Living World seasonal add-ons and packaging the narrative storylines alongside the MMO's expansions instead.
body: Up until today these Living World releases, which act as narrative links between the major beats of the overall tale of Guild Wars 2, have been sold separately from major content expansions. Now, players who buy an expansion like Heart of Thorns will get a Living World season free of charge.

The problem with how this used to work was it meant players who just bought expansions would miss information about what key characters were up to, and major developments would be left largely unexplained. With this new DLC model, you'll be able to get the full picture without forking out extra cash.

Those who own the base game get season one of Living World, while those who buy the game's first expansion Heart of Thorns receive Living World season two. Seasons three and four are packaged alongside the Path of Fire expansion, while the final Living World season comes with End of Dragons. Any missing episodes from these Living World seasons are automatically added to accounts who own the aforementioned expansions.

articles.title: Hideo Kojima Defends 2026’s Most Divisive Movie, Likens It to Metal Gear Solid 2
articles.summary: People can't stop talking about Digger, the latest Tom Cruise film from director Alejandro G. Iñárritu. Depending on who you ask, it is either a bloated and self-aggrandizing mess or one of the most insightful and relevant films in years.
body: That army now includes noted cinephile Hideo Kojima who likens Digger to one of his own controversial works.

The creator of the Metal Gear and Death Stranding series finally posted one of his long posts on X detailing his thoughts on the film, and he had nothing less than praise for Iñárritu's latest. " Digger is a film that all of us living in today’s world should see. It is a work that remains with the audience, provoking reflection and sounding alarms," Kojima wrote. But that's only the beginning, as Gizmodo Japan has published an interview with Kojima and Iñárritu in conversation with each other.

articles.title: Ubisoft Shuts Down Beloved 26-Year-Old Studio, Cuts 'Black Flag' Remake Devs
articles.summary: As the video game industry continues to flounder, Ubisoft has announced its latest round of layoffs and closures. The publisher is shutting down the Finnish studio RedLynx, best known for the motorcycle racing series Trials.
body: “Today, we informed our teams of a proposal to close RedLynx in Finland, subject to the local change negotiation process, which would affect up to 52 positions,” Ubisoft said in a leaked statement seen by Eurogamer. “At Ubisoft Singapore, 70 positions have been impacted to align the studio with upcoming production needs. The studio remains an important part of Ubisoft’s global production organisation.”

Ubisoft Singapore's Assassin’s Creed: Black Flag Resynced received critical praise and sold over 3 million copies within its first week. The game hit 99,000 concurrent players on Steam, becoming the largest debut in franchise history. Before that, Ubisoft Singapore worked on Skull and Bones, the poorly received pirate game that went through a lengthy, troubled development cycle.

“We deeply value the contributions of both teams and recognise the impact this may have on our colleagues,” Ubisoft added. “We are committed to supporting our teams throughout this process and conducting it with care and respect.”

articles.title: "This non-profit will be the 'voice of the gamers'" - Former Disco Elysium devs break new ground with player- and developer-owned studio structure
articles.summary: Elsewhere on the site, you can read a big reveal piece that outlines the new game from former Disco Elysium devs under the name of Summer Eternal - an "incendiary RPG" fusing the best bits of text-heavy isometric role-playing games with the world-building and player agency of an immersive sim.
body: But here's the most intriguing part, as far as I'm concerned: the developers are giving you the chance to have a say over how the company is run. If you buy anything from the studio - including the 500 page Anthology that was formally announced today - you are welcome to join the Players Non-Profit community organisation, which owns 5 percent of Summer Eternal and takes part in the studio's governance.

"The Players Non-Profit owns a five percent share in our studio. The other 95 percent is divided between other stakeholders: full-time workers, freelancers and investors in Summer Eternal," explains the studio in a press release. But what exactly does that mean? Well, it's a long and complicated explanation - as these things often are - but the central point is this: every player is a member of the board.

articles.title: GTA 6 leaker's latest video allegedly shows scenes from the final mission, as they indicate the leaks may have come to an end
articles.summary: Cyberleek, the leaker who's been releasing footage from Grand Theft Auto 6 for weeks now, is seemingly done posting leaks. Cyberleek released a new - seemingly final - video today which supposedly shows parts of the game's ending.
body: The leaker has indicated they may be done sharing footage as their goal of pumping their crypto coin had failed. Cyberleek recently said they'd release a 200GB build of the game if the coin hits $30m market cap, which it's nowhere near doing.

The coin has crashed in recent weeks after a major bump that coincided with the release of leaked footage showing co-protagonist Lucia fully naked, shortly after they released footage of co-protagonist Jason also nude.

Eurogamer has seen the latest footage, and it's not as dramatic as Cyberleek initially made it out to be. The footage does not appear to be of the game's ending sequence or final cutscene, though the location of where the action takes place could be a spoiler. The four-minute video ends with a montage of various locations and flyover footage of a city, set to Journey's Don't Stop Believin'.
There may be something there, but when viewed without proper context, it's hard to say what's actually being spoiled. Still, the footage is best avoided if you want to jump into the game fresh.

videos.title: The Witcher 3 Remastered - PS5/PS5 Pro/Xbox X|S Tech Review - Patch 5.01 Frame-Rate Boosts Tested
videos.summary: Digital Foundry is now fully independent! Join the DF Supporter Program and support the team:
body: Despite a rocky launch the Remastered version of The Witcher 3 is gradually improving with each patch on PS5 and Xbox - taking us up to update 5.01. Compared to the initial 5.00 version frame-rates are improved, particularly on both PlayStation consoles. Elsewhere, Tom takes a look at the broader visual upgrades in the remaster, alongside the Pro enhancements. NOTE: Hotfix 5.01b has landed since this video's creation, which CDPR promises to bring "various stability improvements to help ensure a more reliable experience while witchering across the Continent."
